text:
IncidentBot: PAGER — AurumFin private-vpc: elevated 5xx across regional ingress (us-west-2) and sporadic connection drops to tenant NLBs. Paging @net-oncall and oncall SREs. 

Rita Chen: on it. pulling metrics, can someone grab the aurum tenant target-group health?

Sam Ortiz: I see a spike in 503/504 starting 2026-03-15T10:38:06Z, error rate ~27% for /api/v2 on aurum-prod, baseline 120 rps. DNS TTLs 60s.

Alan B: quick check: NLB target health shows failing checks in two AZs. running: 
```bash
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:111222333:targetgroup/aurum-prod-tg/abcd1234
```
output: 3/6 targets unhealthy, reason: "Health checks failing (read timeout)".

Emily G: I just got a note from customer support channel — AurumFin ops were rolling out a firewall rule change around 10:30 UTC that touches SGs in their VPC. possible SG lock-down preventing health probes from our ALB/NLB health ip ranges.

Rita Chen: ok, if healthchecks blocked that's consistent. Is this limited to ingress (customer->our endpoints) or egress too? metrics show increased downstream queueing from dedicated workers.

Mike SRE: looking at flow logs — we see RSTs from IGW subnets to our health-check IP prefixes. customer SG appears to have removed 10.20.0.0/16 (internal prefix) from allowed ingress.

Aurum Support Bot: Customer ticket #AUR-4521: "Emergency maintenance - tightened inbound rules" created at 2026-03-15T10:27Z. Contact: ops@aurum.example.com.

Sam Ortiz: interim mitigation options: 
- ask customer to revert SG change (fast but requires customer ops)
- shift DNS weighted routing to failover ALB in us-east-1 (we control the weight)
- temporarily open health-check ports via security group exception from our prefix list (if customer approves)

Rita Chen: escalation path: @net-oncall please engage customer network lead, request immediate SG rollback or whitelist health-check prefix. I'll start failover plan in parallel.

Alan B: preparing DNS weight shift. current Route53 record: 
```json
{"Name": "api.aurum.example.com", "Type": "A", "Weights": {"us-west-2": 1.0}}
```
I'll change to: 
```json
{"Weights": {"us-west-2": 0.2, "us-east-1": 0.8}}
```
and monitor errors.

Emily G: note — the failover ALB handles the same model pool but sits in a different VPC peering path. it has headroom for +40% traffic. expect some session affinity breaks but better than 5xx.

Mike SRE: while DNS shifts, I'll open a temporary security-rule exception on our side to accept health-check responses and drop nothing. If customer refuses, we can do traffic steering only.

Aurum Support Bot: Customer acknowledged, ops@aurum.example.com says they can revert SG within 20-30m but need us to do immediate mitigation until then.

Rita Chen: executing DNS weight change now. Alan, make the change and post Route53 change-id.

Alan B: updated weights. Change-ID: Z3P4LPM8EXAMPLE. TTL respected 60s. Monitoring logs.

Sam Ortiz: within 90s we see latency drop for failover ALB and error rate trending down: 27% -> 4% -> 0.6% over 8 minutes.

Emily G: customer confirms they rolled back the SG change. they allowed the health-check prefix and restored previous rules at 2026-03-15T10:55Z.

Mike SRE: validated: NLB target health recovered to 100% at 2026-03-15T10:58Z. metrics: error rate back to 0.3% and latency normalized.

Rita Chen: great. reversing DNS weight to prefer us-west-2 gradually 80% -> 100% over 5 minutes to avoid flaps. Alan, please push change when ready.

Alan B: ramping weights to us-west-2=0.8 at Change-ID: Z3REVERSE111. Then to 1.0.

Sam Ortiz: monitoring post-shift, no regression. will keep watch for next 30m.

Emily G: filing incident ticket and marking customer impact: high for 17 minutes, mitigated within 25 minutes via DNS failover + customer rollback. Suggested follow-ups: tighten runbook for customer-driven SG changes, add automated pre-check to block SG delta that would break health-checks.

Mike SRE: action items assigned: 
- Emily: create PM for postmortem + action tracker (#INC-aurum-2026-03-15)
- Alan: add automated health-check preflight to our onboarding docs
- Rita: confirm follow-up call with AurumFin ops

Rita Chen: oncall handoff to Sam in 5. I'm staying on for follow-up. closing note: thanks team, and @Aurum Support Bot please confirm customer CLM ticket updated with mitigation timeline. :thumbsup:

Aurum Support Bot: Ticket AUR-4521 updated with mitigation steps and timeline.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — AurumFin private-vpc ingress/egress errors remediated. Primary cause: customer firewall rule change that inadvertently blocked health probes. Resolution: DNS weighted failover + customer rollback.

Emily G: I'll own the postmortem writeup. putting a placeholder doc in /incidents/postmortems/aurum-2026-03-15.md and assigning reviewers.

Mike SRE: leaving final observation — recommend adding a fail-safe in our routing plane: if NLB target health dips below threshold, auto-weight to verified failover ALB to reduce manual ops.

Rita Chen: noted. thanks all.
